newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Phillips sees more U.S. bank consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Phillips sees more U.S. bank consolidation.

text.p: The U.S. banking industry is likely to continue consolidating without raising antitrust law problems from a decline in competition, Fed Governor Susan Phillips said on Friday.

"Some of our economists have looked at it," Phillips said after a speech at the Atlanta Society of Financial Analysts. "We could have a lot more mergers still and not be running into antitrust problems because the mergers that you're talking about often are across state boundries."
Even as large banks merger, small banks will still be able to thrive, Phillips added.

She declined to respond to questions about the state of the U.S. economy, deferring to Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's upcoming Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress, which she said he would deliver on Feb 26-27.

"We're probably going to end up seeing some nationally based organizations, but there are a lot of people in this country who do like to work with their individual community banks," Phillips said. "So I think that there is still a major niche for smaller banks. I think we'll end up with quite a variety."

The Fed is monitoring the rapid rise in consumer debt, mostly on credit cards, Phillips said. "We do pay a lot of attention to this," she said. "If you look at the relationship of the debt servicing requirements to income streams, we're sort of in the upper end in the range in terms of coverage."

But Phillips signaled that the run-up might be easing. In Fed surveys of bank loan officers "we are seeing that there's been a significant tightening of standards in this area," she said. "I think it has backed off some."
